resources.string: Blocks touches while you ride in the rain. When you lock, RainLock covers the screen with an invisible layer that swallows every touch, and listens for volume-down presses so you can unlock with the button. It does not read what is on your screen. With the one-time permission, RainLock switches this on when you lock and off again when you unlock.
RainLock couldn\'t switch its accessibility service on. Open RainLock and check Setup
No computer needed. But it stays on all the time, which some banking apps object to, and Circle to Search can open for a few seconds after a swipe up
Needs a computer, or Shizuku with Wireless debugging. The service is then on only while locked, and Circle to Search stays blocked after a swipe up

In Accessibility, tap Installed apps → RainLock and turn it on.

If Android says "Restricted setting", tap App info, then ⋮ → Allow restricted settings, and try again.

The catches: it stays on all the time, and some banking apps warn about that or won't open. And Circle to Search is only blocked while the navigation bar is hidden. A swipe up brings the bar back for a few seconds, and holding it then opens Circle to Search.

The one-time permission fixes both.

Lets RainLock switch its accessibility service on only while locked, and keep Circle to Search blocked when a swipe up brings the navigation bar back. It stays granted through updates and reboots.
